claim: Hybrid two-level design (explicit rules over implicit neural layer) reproduces human skill-learning data in CLARION across about 11 tasks, with synergy between levels.
schema_part: S-memory/O (explicit rule layer plus intuitive layer)
agent_test: Ablate: intuitive-only vs rule-only vs both at equal tokens on a rule-discovery task set. Caveat: all evidence comes from Sun's own group.

claim: Explicit rule search hurts when the rule is hard to see (non-salient) and helps when it is salient; instructions help in either case.
schema_part: G (do not force rule hunting on every task)
agent_test: Prompt an explicit 'find the rule' step on salient vs non-salient tasks; measure accuracy at equal tokens. Gap search: LLM analogue measured (Liu 2025): forced CoT on AGL, GPT-4o 87.5 to 64.4; most listed models drop; Claude 3.5 Sonnet does not.

claim: Verbalising a strategy during an interruption lowers insight-problem solving (45.8% to 35.6%, Schooler 1993); CLARION reproduces it.
agent_test: Test forced step-by-step narration vs silent retry on insight puzzles at equal tokens. Verbal overshadowing has a mixed replication record outside this set. Gap search: face verbal overshadowing registered replication gives -4.01% (31 labs) and -16.31% (22 labs) vs original 22-25%; LLM CoT analogue drops on face recognition (GPT-4o 64.0 to 51.2). Insight-narration version still unreplicated in sources opened.

claim: LLM plus symbolic solver beats the LLM alone on logic tasks, but chain of thought wins when the formal translation adds nothing (PrOntoQA: CoT 98.79 vs Logic-LM 83.20, GPT-4).
agent_test: Per-task route: formalise-and-solve vs CoT at equal tokens; log solver execution failures. Gap search: Sprague 2025 shows solver beats CoT on symbolic tasks but CoT adds nothing on non-symbolic ones; a router by task type or draft agreement (DART) is untested on Logic-LM items.

claim: A fast small model with a slow planner called on demand beats single-model agent loops on ScienceWorld at fewer tokens per action (SwiftSage 84.68 vs ReAct 36.43, GPT-4).
schema_part: S/O (fast path default, slow path on trigger)
agent_test: Fast-default with escalation rule vs always-slow at matched total tokens. Hand-written switch rules; one benchmark. Gap search: independent routers (DART, ODAR) also find fast-default routing matches always-slow with 32-73% fewer thinking tokens; ODAR proportion-matched random routing loses 8.3 macro points. SwiftSage itself still has no token-matched ablation.

claim: A code-run metacognitive loop around a small fast LLM, escalating to a reasoning model only on failure, beats the reasoning model alone (graph coloring size 25: 42% vs 2%; DebugBench Python 70% vs 37%).
agent_test: Matched-token comparison of fast+feedback loops (5 rounds) vs one long reasoning call. All from one group (SOFAI).

claim: Most gain from feedback iterations arrives in the first few rounds; what history to pass on is task dependent (graph coloring: problem only; code debugging: best attempt or full history).
agent_test: Sweep rounds 1/5/10 and history modes at equal tokens.

claim: External sound verifiers make LLM generate-and-test planning work (GPT-4 about 12% alone; Blocks World 82% with VAL in 15 rounds) but not on obfuscated domains (about 10%).
agent_test: Same domains, matched tokens, verifier vs self-critique. b19 and c20 are the same paper, so one source. Gap search: Stechly 2024 and Huang 2024 confirm gains need a sound verifier: GPT-4 self-verification Game of 24 3% vs 5% baseline vs 36-38% with sound verifier.

claim: Distilling a slow procedure into direct answers works for some tasks (last letter 30.0 to 98.0%) but fails for chain-of-thought math (GSM8k 9.40 System 1, 52.77 CoT, 7.13 distilled).
agent_test: Not testable by scaffold; informs the limit that intuition cannot absorb multi-step reasoning.

claim: Fast/slow split fails in two ways: an intuitive answer from stale belief, and a snap judgement before the slow module finishes multi-step plans.
agent_test: Count premature-answer errors in an async talker/reasoner agent vs sequential.

claim: Implicit learning (AGL) is real but inflated: pooled g=1.069 over 78 studies, 3,559 subjects, with publication bias (Peters p=.023), shrinking with more training and inflated by item repetition at test.
agent_test: Not a scaffold test; use as caution on human implicit-learning claims.

claim: Trust in intuition does not track actual implicit-learning performance (r=-.05, BF01=6.02).
schema_part: G (do not weight by felt confidence)
agent_test: Compare confidence-weighted vs verifier-weighted selection at equal tokens. Gap search: self-reported confidence routing (MC-Conf) trails draft-agreement routing; vote and reward-model selection saturate near 41% on MATH while coverage reaches 98% (Large Language Monkeys). No direct felt-confidence vs verifier selection test found.

claim: Base LLMs behave like fast intuitive responders on cognitive-reflection items and newer chat models shift to chain of thought (CRT correct: davinci-003 5%, GPT-3.5 59%, GPT-4 96%, humans 38%).
agent_test: Run CRT-style items with and without a slow-path prompt.

claim: Position papers argue LLMs fill CLARION's implicit level while explicit rules, motivation and metacognition must be added; no controlled test exists.
agent_test: Implement veto/validate loop (b07 four-step creative loop) and measure vs plain prompting. All are Sun's own position papers. Gap search: no controlled test of the LLM = implicit level claim, but measured LLM plus symbolic-runtime systems exist (NL2GenSym on Soar: 55% to 86% over one-shot; SCALAR: 88.2% vs 46.9%). Rosenbloom 2024-2025 papers opened: conceptual only.

claim: The Standard Model of the Mind connectivity fits fMRI better than structural-only or fully connected models (N=103, four tasks).
agent_test: Not an agent test.

claim: Sigma shows one mechanism (factor graphs, gradient descent) can do symbolic, probabilistic and neural tasks, but accuracy is modest (POS tagging 90.3% equals the most-common-tag baseline).
agent_test: Not an agent test.

claim: Tight coupling of an LLM to a symbolic architecture inherits LLM hallucination as cascading errors.
agent_test: Rule-extraction memory with and without a check before commit. Gap search: HtT random-rule control shows wrong rules cost 34-41 points; coverage and confidence filter and trajectory feedback (SCALAR 88 to 67% when removed) are the measured guards.

claim: An LLM used as its own verifier or veto layer lowers accuracy; only a sound external verifier (solver, tests, tool) gives gains. GPT-4 Game of 24: standard 5%, LLM+LLM 3%, sound verifier 36-38%.
schema_part: G (veto must be sound; no self-veto without ground truth)
agent_test: Veto by code or retrieved fact vs veto by same-model critique at equal tokens. Tested only on 2023-24 models; reasoning models untested.

claim: Rule extraction into a library helps only when rules are filtered by coverage and confidence; random wrong rules do much more harm than no rules (CLUTRR GPT-4: 50.6 no rules, 64.3 filtered rules, 9.9 random rules).
schema_part: G (validate before commit to rule memory)
agent_test: Rule memory with and without coverage and confidence filter on a task with changing rules.

claim: Forced chain-of-thought lowers LLM accuracy on tasks where verbal thinking hurts humans: AGL GPT-4o 87.5 to 64.4, o1-preview 57.7 vs GPT-4o direct 94.0 (subset), exceptions task 2.9 to 12.5 passes, face recognition 64.0 to 51.2. Not all models drop.
schema_part: G/O (keep a direct-answer path; do not force rule-finding on pattern items)
agent_test: Route pattern or perceptual judgement items to direct answer; compare with forced CoT on the same model.

claim: CoT helps mostly on math, symbolic and logic items (+14.2, +12.3, +6.9 pts) and about 0.7 pts elsewhere; about 95% of MMLU gain is on items with an equals sign. A per-item route by task type is therefore supported.
schema_part: O (route: slow path only for symbolic items)
agent_test: Router by task type vs always-CoT at matched tokens on a mixed set.

claim: No quantitative test of Sigma or the Common Model of Cognition with an LLM exists in sources opened (Rosenbloom 2024-2025 papers are proposals); the nearest measured work uses Soar (NL2GenSym, 55% to 86% on water jugs).
agent_test: Not an agent test.

claim: No independent replication or fit statistics for CLARION human-data fits were found; they stay single-group claims.
agent_test: Not an agent test.
